guide.summary: Private app on your own workspace (self-serve, wait none); Public app for other Intercom customers (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Private app on your own workspace (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app for other Intercom customers (app review).

composio.note: Composio manages OAuth for Intercom, so prototypes need no own app. For launch with your own branding, create a custom auth config with your client ID and secret.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, since Composio provides a managed Intercom app. For production with your brand on the consent screen and a dedicated quota, use your own app, which means Intercom's review for public use.
reasons: Consent screen shows your brand instead of Composio
Dedicated quota instead of quota shared across Composio users
Control over scopes beyond Composio defaults
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval

prerequisites.title: Developer Hub app and paid workspace
prerequisites.detail: Create the app in the Developer Hub. Each development workspace can use OAuth.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS redirect URL
prerequisites.detail: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS. The first one you enter is the default.

prerequisites.title: Test account and demo materials
prerequisites.detail: If your service needs an account, provide test credentials or setup instructions. You also need a video and a short description.

prerequisites.title: Privacy policy and end user agreement
prerequisites.detail: Intercom requires both for each customer, compatible with its terms.

steps.title: Create app and enable OAuth
steps.detail: Log in to the Developer Hub, create the app and tick Use OAuth on the Authentication page.
steps.done_when: client_id and client_secret visible on Basic Information page

steps.title: Draft minimal scope list
steps.detail: Pick only the scopes the use case needs and write a justification for each.

steps.title: Set redirect URL and scopes
steps.detail: Enter the HTTPS redirect URL and tick the scopes in the Developer Hub.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a custom auth config via Composio's API with your client ID and secret. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard. Because Composio's callback domain can't be verified by you, you may route it through your own domain with a 302 redirect.
steps.done_when: Auth config created and a test connection works

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Show OAuth install, full app functionality and OAuth uninstall, with full client_id and state visible in the OAuth URL. Show more rather than less.

steps.title: Complete listing and partner forms
steps.detail: Fill in company details, use cases and contacts; for App Store listing also complete listing fields and Installation status links.

steps.title: Submit for review
steps.detail: Submit the app to the Intercom team.

steps.title: Wait for Intercom review
steps.detail: Review can take up to seven business days. Resubmission after changes can take the same.

steps.title: Optionally list in App Store
steps.detail: Select List in App store on the listing page to go live for public installs.

traps.title: Over-privileged scopes cause rejection
traps.detail: This is the most common initial rejection reason. Request only the scopes you need.

traps.title: Incomplete video forces resubmission
traps.detail: If the video lacks full functionality or the OAuth processes, you must resubmit it.

traps.title: Broken installation links reject the app
traps.detail: Broken or unclear links cause rejection and resubmission.

traps.title: Naming and logo rules
traps.detail: The app name cannot contain Intercom and must be unique. The icon cannot contain the Intercom logo.

traps.title: Wrong region host fails for Google sign-in
traps.detail: Using the US host for an EU or AU customer prompts region choice, but fails if they sign in with Google.

traps.title: Managed app shows Composio branding
traps.detail: Users see Composio on the consent screen and share quota with other Composio users.

blockers.symptom: Rejection for scopes outside the app's functionality
blockers.what_it_means: Requested scopes exceed what the app does.
blockers.what_to_do: Reduce scopes and resubmit; you can discard pending submitted changes to edit.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare scopes to features and propose a smaller list.

blockers.symptom: Rejected for broken links or images
blockers.what_it_means: Installation links or listing images did not meet requirements.
blockers.what_to_do: Fix links and use marketing-format images, then resubmit.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check image sizes and link validity against listing requirements.

open_questions: Which specific scopes get extra scrutiny? Docs give only a general scope review; ask Intercom developer support.
Actual review time in practice: no community-reported wait found; ask Intercom support or the developer community.
Do customer admins need to approve the app? Not stated in the docs; check with Intercom support.
Any OAuth API fees or plan requirements for customers? Docs do not state; check Intercom pricing.

evidence.answer: The video should show too much of the app rather than too little; if not all functionality and OAuth processes are shown, the video must be resubmitted.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Write a brief description of your app and how it works with Intercom.
evidence.answer: The developer must write a brief app description of how the app works with Intercom.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: In order to access your app we will need to test out the full functionality. This means if your app requires a subscription or account with your service, you'll need to provide us with test account credentials or set up instructions within the description.
evidence.answer: If the app needs a subscription or account with the developer's service, the developer must provide test account credentials or setup instructions so the full functionality can be tested.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Please ensure that you have met the requirements for the App Store listing — one common pitfall is submitting images that are not in marketing format.
evidence.answer: Listed apps must meet the App Store listing requirements, and submitting images not in marketing format is a common pitfall.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Providing broken or unclear links will result in an application rejection, and you will have to resubmit for review.
evidence.answer: Broken or unclear installation links in the Installation status section cause the app to be rejected and require resubmission.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: This form asks for information including your company details, target use cases, points of contact, and more.
evidence.answer: The App Partner Program form asks for company details, target use cases, points of contact, and more.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: If you have requested scopes outside of the current functionality, you may be asked to adjust your scopes and resubmit the app.
evidence.answer: Requesting scopes beyond the app's current functionality may require the developer to adjust scopes and resubmit the app.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: During this process, your app will be **private** and can only be used by you and your team.
evidence.answer: Before approval, an app is private and usable only by the developer and their team, not by outside customers.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: You will see a yellow banner at the top of the screen stating it can take up to seven business days for review.
evidence.answer: The page says a review can take up to seven business days.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: Your application can take up to seven business days to review, so ensure everything is fixed.
evidence.answer: A resubmission after rejection can also take up to seven business days to review.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: If you are asked to make changes, you may resubmit your app after making the requested changes and our team will review it further.
evidence.answer: If the app is asked to make changes, it may be resubmitted and the team will review it further.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: However, if you need to make any changes in the future the app will need to be re-approved by the Intercom team.
evidence.answer: After approval, changes to the app require re-approval by the Intercom team.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: However, in cases where an app is updated after it is approved and published, the app will remain public with the current functionality until your updates have been approved.
evidence.answer: For an already published app that is updated, it stays public with its current functionality until the updates are approved.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: This requires filling out the App Listing and App Partner Program pages in the Developer Hub and ensuring that all the requirements for each are met.
evidence.answer: To be listed in the Intercom App Store, the developer must fill out the App Listing and App Partner Program pages and meet all requirements for each.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You must fill out the Installation status section in order to submit your app to be listed in the App Store.
evidence.answer: The Installation status section must be filled out to submit a listed app for the App Store.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Each development workspace automatically gives you the option to use OAuth.
evidence.answer: Each development workspace automatically gives the developer the option to use OAuth.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: you are required to set up OAuth.
evidence.answer: A public integration that accesses other people's Intercom data must set up OAuth.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: It's best practice as these will go up for review when you
evidence.answer: Requested scopes go up for review when the developer submits the app for review.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: After approval, you can choose which URL to use when you're initiating the OAuth flow via the `redirect_uri` parameter.
evidence.answer: The page refers to an approval that happens before the redirect URI can be chosen for the OAuth flow.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: It's best practice as these will go up for review when you
evidence.answer: The page does not describe what a review checks, but it says the requested scopes are what goes up for review.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: You should only specify the scopes you definitely need for your use case.
evidence.answer: Developers should request only the scopes they definitely need for their use case, since those scopes go up for review.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: The following scopes will be automatically selected and cannot be deselected:
evidence.answer: Apps using Canvas Kit have four scopes automatically selected that cannot be deselected: read and list users and companies, read conversations, read admins, and gather App data.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: The following permissions can be selected via checkboxes on your Authorization page:
evidence.answer: The page lists standard people and conversation scopes (e.g., Read conversations: View conversations) selectable by checkbox on the Authorization page.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Read and write AI content | Create and update AI content
evidence.answer: The page lists extended workspace scopes such as Read and write AI content (create and update AI content).

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Webhook topics are related to corresponding permission scopes
evidence.answer: Webhook topics are tied to permission scopes; for example, user/lead-created webhooks require the 'Read and write users' scope.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: do not need to set up OAuth.
evidence.answer: For a private app that only needs data from the developer's paid Intercom workspace, OAuth setup is not needed and Access Tokens can be used instead; the page does not state OAuth API fees.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Your user will be presented with the permissions that your app is requesting.
evidence.answer: The end user is shown the permissions the app requests and must approve them before being redirected back.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Once the user approves this request, they are redirected back via the Redirect URLs which you provided earlier.
evidence.answer: After the user approves the request, they are redirected back to the developer's Redirect URLs.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS
evidence.answer: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: so the URL will need to be over HTTPS.
evidence.answer: The redirect must go over a TLS/SSL connection, so the URL must be HTTPS.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: This is the URL which we POST to when your user has authorized your app to access their information.
evidence.answer: The redirect URL is where Intercom sends the authorization code after the user authorizes the app.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: The first will always be the default.
evidence.answer: Developers can add multiple redirect URLs, and the first one entered is the default.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: This means you can include testing as well as production URLs here.
evidence.answer: After approval, the developer can choose which redirect URL to use via the redirect_uri parameter, so testing and production URLs can both be listed.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: To start, tick the **Use OAuth** option on your Authentication page in the Developer Hub.
evidence.answer: To start, the developer ticks the Use OAuth option on the Authentication page in the Developer Hub.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: You'll now have two sections to fill out:
evidence.answer: After enabling OAuth, two sections must be filled out: Redirect URLs and Permissions.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: You'll first need your `client_id` and `client_secret`. These can be found on the Basic Information page for your app in the Developer Hub.
evidence.answer: The client_id and client_secret are found on the Basic Information page for the app in the Developer Hub.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: https://app.intercom.com/oauth?client_id=___&state=___
evidence.answer: The US authorization endpoint is https://app.intercom.com/oauth with client_id and state parameters.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Intercom hosts workspaces in three regions, and each region has its own authorization host.
evidence.answer: Intercom hosts workspaces in three regions, each with its own authorization host.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: One exception: if the customer signs in with Google, the wrong regional host fails rather than prompting, so matching the region is required in that case.
evidence.answer: Using the default US host for an EU or AU customer makes them choose their region on the sign-in page, but if they sign in with Google the wrong regional host fails.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: A random session specific string which we will return in the callback
evidence.answer: The state value is a random session-specific string returned in the callback to identify the session and mitigate CSRF attacks.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The request to your Redirect URL will have 2 URL parameters: `code` and `state`.
evidence.answer: The redirect back to the developer's Redirect URL includes code and state parameters.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: We can now exchange the `code` for the Access Token with a POST request to:
evidence.answer: The authorization code is exchanged for an access token with a POST request to https://api.intercom.io/auth/eagle/token.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: `client_id`: Your app's Client ID from the Developer Hub (see above)
evidence.answer: The token exchange body requires the code, client_id, and client_secret from the Developer Hub.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: `token_type`: Always 'Bearer'
evidence.answer: A successful token response has token_type always 'Bearer', plus token and access_token (a duplicate of the token).

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack. You do not need to register your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Composio registers and maintains its own OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack (the page does not name Intercom).

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Custom auth configs: You provide your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.
evidence.answer: With a custom auth config, the developer supplies their own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tells Composio to use them for a toolkit.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users. Your own app gets a dedicated quota.
evidence.answer: Managed apps share their quota across all Composio users, while a developer's own app gets a dedicated quota.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; a developer's own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.
evidence.answer: With managed apps, users see 'Composio wants to access your account' during OAuth rather than the developer's app name.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need (e.g., write access to a specific Google API).
evidence.answer: Composio's default scopes for managed apps may not include everything a developer needs, for example write access to a specific Google API.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: To check whether Composio provides the OAuth app for a toolkit, see [Managed OAuth apps](/toolkits/managed-auth).
evidence.answer: Managed apps are the default when available, and the developer can check whether Composio provides the OAuth app for a given toolkit on the Managed OAuth apps page.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: During OAuth, the browser briefly redirects through `backend.composio.dev` so Composio can capture the auth token.
evidence.answer: During OAuth, the browser briefly redirects through Composio's backend domain so Composio can capture the auth token.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Some toolkits also display this URL on the consent screen.
evidence.answer: Some toolkits also display Composio's callback URL on the consent screen.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: If you need to hide Composio's domain, you can proxy the redirect through your own domain instead.
evidence.answer: To hide Composio's domain, you can proxy the redirect through your own domain instead.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: In your OAuth app's settings, set the authorized redirect URI to your own endpoint:
evidence.answer: In your own OAuth app's settings, you set the authorized redirect URI to your own endpoint, for example https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: This endpoint receives the OAuth callback and immediately 302-redirects it to Composio:
evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint on your domain receives the OAuth callback and immediately 302-redirects it to Composio.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Your endpoint must return a **302 redirect**. Do not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio.
evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint must return a 302 redirect, and must not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: "Composio wants to access your account" on Google, GitHub, etc.
evidence.answer: Without your own OAuth app, the provider's consent screen shows "Composio wants to access your account" (for example on Google, GitHub, etc.).

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Add your own OAuth app only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.
evidence.answer: You should add your own OAuth app only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: composio_url = "https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback"
evidence.answer: When proxying, the callback URL registered in your OAuth app is your own endpoint, which forwards to Composio's callback URL https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback.
